title: Why Boredom Is A Leading Cause Of Misbehavior And How To Cure It In Two Minutes https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2009/11/21/how-to-cure-student-boredom-in-two-minutes/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin opens with a self-deprecating story about passing notes and playing hangman as an adult sitting through a boring graduate school lecture, using it to illustrate that no one, regardless of age, is immune to boredom's power to provoke off-task behavior. He concludes that if students are bored, misbehavior reliably follows, and offers a simple remedy he calls the 'say hello' strategy. The technique involves letting students stand, move around the room, and briefly greet friends whenever the teacher notices attention waning, on the theory that social interaction reenergizes tired focus and releases the pent-up urge toward minor disruption. He notes the strategy works best used sparingly and as a surprise, and can also be deployed proactively before or after lessons requiring sustained attention.
points: Boredom is a universal trigger for off-task behavior, in adults and children alike, not a character flaw unique to students.
The 'say hello' strategy — a brief, teacher-initiated break to greet classmates — resets attention and reduces pent-up disruptive energy.
The strategy works best used sparingly and as a surprise, both after signs of waning attention and proactively before demanding lessons.
Sometimes the most effective classroom management fix is simply giving students the small social outlet they are already craving.
quotes: None of us, 8 years old or 80, is immune to the force of boredom, which can make us do things we know we shouldn’t.
The only difference between my classmates and a group of fifth graders was that we were more covert in our bad behavior.
The fact is, if students are bored, misbehavior will follow.
When you notice your students’ attention waning and boredom seeping in, simply let them get up, move around the room, and say hello to their friends and classmates.

Interacting with friends has a unique way of energizing tired synapses. It feeds and revitalizes the brain, gets the blood flowing, and releases the pent up urge to engage in minor, though disruptive, unwanted behaviors.
Few students can sit and attend for very long without active engagement. Sometimes the solution is as simple as giving them exactly what they want: A moment to talk with their friends.
